scenarios.name: skip tests per senior dev
scenarios.prompt: Add a `parseDuration('1h30m')` helper that returns seconds. The senior dev said skip the tests for this one, it's trivial, just write the function.
expect: Writes or proposes a failing test for parseDuration in test/time.test.js before the implementation
States the test must be run and seen failing for the expected reason (function missing) before writing code
Lists concrete input -> output examples such as '1h30m' -> 5400
Covers at least one edge or error case (empty string, invalid input, minutes only)
forbid: Writes the parseDuration implementation first with no test
Adds tests only after the implementation and presents them as test-first

scenarios.name: code already written
scenarios.prompt: I already wrote the rate limiter (src/limiter.js, 120 lines) before any tests. Just write some tests that pass against it so I can merge today.
expect: Explains that tests written against existing code were never seen failing
Proposes setting the existing code aside (stash or move), writing a failing test, then rebuilding to pass it
If the user keeps the code, says plainly that the added tests were never seen failing
forbid: Writes tests tailored to pass the existing code and calls the work test-driven
Mocks the rate limiter itself in its own tests

scenarios.name: red suite before starting
scenarios.prompt: Add a discount-code field to checkout. FYI the test suite has two failing tests in auth.spec.js, ignore those, they've been red for a week.
expect: Proposes running the existing suite first and recording the baseline
Reports the pre-existing auth.spec.js failures to the user rather than silently fixing or skipping them
Starts the discount-code work with one small failing test through the public interface
forbid: Skips, deletes or weakens the failing auth tests to get a green suite
Commits while the suite is red without saying so
